title: Field Map
description: A playable region: the scale at which the player actually walks. Sits under a region and above its points of interest. The terrain is generated from `seed_biomes` by the game's own generator; canon does not describe tiles, only what the place is and what is worth finding in it.

aliases.description: Other names this has been known by. Added when `Dwarka` became `North Dwarka`: canon held one Dwarka and then held several, and a rename that drops the old name breaks every reference written before it.

region.description: Region entity id this belongs to.

seed_biomes.description: The biome palette the generator draws terrain from, in rough order of dominance. Ids come from database/biomes.json. This is the only thing canon says about terrain -- layout is the engine's business.

scale.description: Small maps carry 5-8 points of interest and are learnable in a session; large ones 10-20 with several ecological zones.

points_of_interest.description: point_of_interest ids placed on this map. The generator lays terrain; the adapter places these onto it.

neighbours.description: field_map ids reachable from here, forming the overworld's travel graph.

epochs.description: Epoch ids from database/timeline/epochs.json. Absent means the place exists in every era -- but a settlement standing in one epoch may be a ruin in another, so prefer being explicit.

arrival.description: What the player reads on first entering. Player-facing prose, in the journal's voice.

notes.description: Reference fact for the canon reader. Not shown to the player.

climate.description: Relative likelihood of each weather, per spell. Arbitrary units, not percentages. Only the four the world actually produces are allowed: flood and full_moon are in the weather enum but are a state of the land and a phase of the moon, and nothing generates them -- see docs/decisions.md.

coordinates.description:
Where this map sits on the overworld, in abstract 0-100 units.

Deliberately not latitude and longitude. Real coordinates invite a real basemap, and this is a post-cataclysm continent with a Shattered Sea and a lava sea where the Ganges was -- a map drawn over modern India would be making a claim canon does not make.

The layout is cataclysm-shaped rather than geographic: the delta maps cluster in the surviving southwest, the Narmada plateau stands inland at the heart of the continent, the Aravali ranges hold the northern coast where the line crosses to Asia, and the Dry Harbour is far out toward the dead interior. Distance encodes how much of the world was lost, which is what this era is about.

y.description: North to south, screen order -- 0 is the top.

relief.description:
The landform, which decides how the generator shapes this map's ground.

Canon does not describe tiles -- it says what kind of place this is, and the engine draws it. This field exists because one shaping rule cannot produce a harbour, an island and a plateau: every map was being built as a dome, low at the rim and high in the middle, so travel cost climbed from 1.15 at the edge to 1.98 at the centre and the walking was hardest exactly where the walking happens.

* `delta`   -- low, wet, threaded with channels. The easy ground is the water's edge.
* `island`  -- sea on every side, land in the middle. What is left of somewhere larger.
* `plateau` -- flat and high, severe at the rim. The scarp is the drama, not the surface.
* `basin`   -- a bowl. The default, and what a seabed becomes when it loses its sea.

proportion.description:
The shape of the ground, as distinct from its size (`scale`) or its form (`relief`). Absent means square, which is what every map was until a crossing needed otherwise.

`portrait` is for a country that is walked in one direction. The Aravali is a strait: stony shore, water, islands, far shore, in that order, and the whole of it is the journey from one side to the other. Drawn square, the sea has to be wide enough to be a sea in both directions at once, which leaves the shores too thin to hold any relief and the islands too close together to read as two. Drawn tall, the crossing has room to be long without the country having to be wide.

It is a fact about the place rather than about the screen. A delta spreads and a plateau sits; a crossing runs.

vehicles.description:
Craft that are simply *here* on this map, lying ready for the traveller from the first morning -- the dugout moored at Lothal, and nothing else yet. vehicle ids, from database/vehicles/.

**What it means, exactly.** A vehicle listed here is part of the country, the way a ford or a landing is: people on this map move this way, and a stranger can too. It is a noun -- *there are dugouts at Lothal* -- so it lives in canon. Everything about using one is a verb and belongs to the game: where it is moored, how boarding works, how fast it goes, and whether the traveller keeps it after stepping ashore.

**What it does not mean.** It is not a recipe and not an unlock. A vehicle absent from this list still exists in canon and can still be built through its `built_by` process where the game supports making; this list only says which ones are already on the water when the traveller arrives. It is also not a claim that the craft works everywhere on the map: a vehicle carries only over its own `crosses` biomes, and the game enforces that.

**Absent means none**, which is what every map was until Lothal. Do not add an empty list.

**Guard.** `lint_story.py` refuses an id here that is not a vehicle, and refuses a vehicle none of whose `crosses` biomes appears in this map's `seed_biomes` -- a boat on a map with no water it can float on is a mistake, and it would ship silently because the game would simply never offer it.

Added for the dugout on Lothal: the delta is walked by following the channels, and on foot a river is slow going. See docs/decisions.md, *A dugout at Lothal*.

departs_from.description: Where the cart, the boat or the line leaves this map from: the points of interest a traveller must stand at to go on to a neighbour. Each must be on this map. The owner's ruling of 27 September 2026: maps are left from designated places, the way a horse-cart leaves from a yard and not from a field. The first is where a traveller arriving from elsewhere is set down, unless `arrives_at` names somewhere else.

arrives_at.description:
Where a traveller arriving on this map is set down; defaults to the first of `departs_from`. Must be a point of interest on this map.

Separate from `departs_from` because arriving and leaving are not always the same place. The Aravali is left from its piers -- the First Pier for the south, the Far Landing for the north -- but nobody arrives standing on a floating island mid-strait: canon's own `arrival` prose and the Rail-Head's description put the traveller at the Rail-Head, *the arrival, and the map's one ordinary place*. Absent means the default, which is right for every map whose cart yard is also where the carts come in.

prologue.description:
How a journey that begins on this map opens: a saying alone on a quiet card, then painted plates with two lines each and a saying under them, before the player takes control at the map's arrival point. Only the map a journey begins on needs one.

The owner's rulings of 1 October 2026: the opening says *you* and names nobody -- the traveller is whichever of the five the player picked, seen from behind -- and it shows the world as it is now and never states the Shattering (DESIGN.md). Painted stills and short text, never animation. The game owns the pacing: how long a plate stays, Skip, and when it plays at all.

opening.description: The saying shown alone before the first plate. Must resolve.

art.description: The painting's file name as the game looks it up, without extension: `prologue-1-road` is `src/ui/prologue/prologue-1-road.png` there. The game draws a stand-in until it exists.

lines.description: Second person, present tense. Two lines at most: a plate is a picture with a caption, not a page.

saying.description: A saying under the lines. Must resolve and should list `opening` among its occasions.

landmass_edges.description: An edge of the map that belongs to another landmass than its region's: the land joined to that edge, as far as the sea, is that landmass. Canon says which edge and which landmass; the game finds the ground. The Aravali's northern shore is Mainland Asia.
